discovery: Optical detection and coherent control of single spins in diamond and their development into nanoscale quantum sensors
subfield: Quantum science and technology / solid-state spin physics
motivation: Wrachtrup first optically detected magnetic resonance of a single nitrogen-vacancy defect in diamond and showed coherent control of single electron and nuclear spins at room temperature. That turned an isolated quantum spin in a solid into an object that can be read out and manipulated. Lukin and Walsworth showed that these single spins work as atomic-scale magnetometers, and with Wrachtrup they made NV magnetometry a widely used quantum-sensing platform. It has reached nanoscale NMR, imaging of magnetism and current flow in condensed-matter systems, single-cell biological magnetic imaging, and spin-photon entanglement for quantum networks. Their work opened a new field: engineered solid-state spin defects as qubits and sensors. It inspired a search for spin qubit hosts across wide-bandgap materials, and hundreds of laboratories and industry now use it.
